name: ai-summary-must-match-actual-code
body:
When documenting a function or mechanism in @ai-summary, verify the described behavior actually exists in the code. The invalidatePublishedInteractiveLessonPrompt() function was documented as being called by a Prompts hook, but grep across the entire src/ tree showed zero callers — the function exists but has no hook wiring it. This is a correctness-level bug in documentation.

**Both module-level AND function-level JSDoc must be checked.** The prior PR fixed the module-level @ai-summary but overlooked the function-level JSDoc on the same function, leaving the stale claim in place at lines 70-73. Any reader who reads the function directly still encounters the false claim.

**Why:** @ai-summary is consumed by AI agents to understand code behavior. False documentation leads to incorrect assumptions, wasted investigation, and broken tool use.

**How to apply:** Before finalizing an @ai-summary that describes hook-based or event-driven behavior, grep the codebase for the function/hook name to confirm it is actually invoked. Check both the module-level and function-level JSDoc when making such fixes.
why: published-prompt-cache.ts @ai-summary claimed a hook calls invalidatePublishedInteractiveLessonPrompt(), but the function has zero callers — verified by cross-file grep. The module-level fix was correct but function-level JSDoc was overlooked.

name: verbatim-ai-summary-duplication
hook: Same gotcha wording in multiple @ai-summary headers should be independently phrased
body:
When the same gotcha appears in multiple files (e.g. Gemini's responseSchema issue #1748), each @ai-summary should phrase it independently rather than copying verbatim text. Two files with identical wording suggest cut-and-paste rather than independent documentation.

**Why:** Verbatim duplication across files suggests the wording was copied rather than each author understanding the constraint independently. Unique phrasing demonstrates genuine knowledge transfer.

**How to apply:** When documenting the same behavior in multiple files, rephrase the gotcha independently in each location — keep the meaning but use different words.
why: lesson-duplication-variation-service.ts and lesson-duplication-output.ts both had 'collapses nested object arrays into literal string arrays (issue #1748)' verbatim; independently rephrased to avoid the appearance of copy-paste documentation.
